key_insight: The Critical 2D KPZ Process provides a nontrivial, distribution-valued solution to the two-dimensional KPZ equation at criticality.
engineering_relevance: The work offers a mathematical foundation for critical stochastic growth models, rather than a demonstrated AI-driven materials discovery method.
method: Take limits in law of centred log partition functions for critical two-dimensional Gaussian directed polymers.
Apply a renormalised Cole–Hopf transformation to spatially mollified Critical 2D Stochastic Heat Flow.
Characterise covariance singularities and fluctuations under shrinking-scale spatial averaging.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports mathematical results establishing a non-Gaussian process, log-log covariance blow-up near the diagonal, and Gaussian fluctuations under local averaging; it provides no experimental or materials benchmarks.
watch_item: The solution is distribution-valued and requires renormalisation; direct numerical or materials-engineering applicability is not established in the abstract.
